previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of MSSA bacteremia and C. difficile infection was admitted for a recurrent gastroparesis flare characterized by nausea, vomiting, and abdominal discomfort. Her symptoms were likely triggered by severe hyperglycemia and significant fluid overload, with labs showing glucose of 699 and hyponatremia (Na 123). She was managed with bowel rest, insulin therapy, and two hemodialysis sessions for fluid removal, which led to marked improvement in symptoms and electrolyte balance. Her blood cultures remained negative, and her MSSA bacteremia prophylaxis with cefazolin and vancomycin locks was continued. She completed her metronidazole course for C. difficile and was discharged home in stable condition, tolerating a full diet, with instructions to maintain strict fluid restriction and continue outpatient antibiotic and diabetes management.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted to the hospital with DKA.  You were briefly 
treated with an insulin drip in the intensive care unit.  It 
seems like the cause of the DKA was the fact that your insulin 
dosing was inadequate, because even after the DKA resolved you 
continued to have high sugars on your home regimen.  Therefore, 
we adjusted your insulin dosing as follows:
1. Lantus increased to 10units in the morning, 14units at night 
(your previous dose was 8unit in the morning, 10 units at night)
2. Humalog sliding scale:
--- Give yourself 4 units of Humalog before each meal, 
regardless of your pre-meal finger stick
--- Use a sliding scale to adjust your pre-meal fingerstick 
which increased by one unit for increasing by one unit for every 
50 over 150 (for example 5 units for 150-200, 6 units for 
201-250, etc)

Some information about your other medical problems:
1. Bloodstream infection with MSSA: you will continue getting an 
antibiotic called cefazolin after dialysis until ___. You will 
continue getting vancomycin locks for the port until ___.
2. C. Diff (bowel infection causing diarrhea): you will continue 
taking flagyl (also called metronidazole) 800mg three times a 
day until ___.
3. High blood pressure: your blood pressure was persistently 
high; therefore, your labetalol was increased to 800mg three 
times a day (the dose used to be 600mg three times a day).

It was a pleasure taking care of you and we wish you all the 
best.
Sincerely, 
Your ___ Team
